what: Logitech makes the things attached to a computer: mice, keyboards, webcams, headsets, and gaming gear under the Logitech G and Astro names, plus video conferencing equipment for meeting rooms.
customers: Consumers buying through retailers and online, gamers, and companies fitting out meeting rooms.
money: mice, keyboards, headsets and racing wheels
moat: Shelf space and brand recognition in a category most buyers choose by name, supported by a design and distribution operation that smaller rivals cannot match.
risks: Revenue fell from $5.5B to $4.3B after the pandemic surge and has only partly recovered
Peripherals are replaced slowly and the purchase is easy to postpone
Manufacturing in China exposes the cost base to tariffs
opportunities: $953M of free cash flow and $1.7B of cash against $88M of debt, on a $14.1B market value
A 14.7% net margin, unusually high for consumer hardware, because the brand supports its prices
Revenue has grown for two years running, from $4.3B to $4.8B
watch: Gaming segment sales and whether the video collaboration business returns to growth.
